about: Grouping SQL check cases. Inspire App lib/groupingSql.js checkGroupingSql and the agent notebook implement_grouping_sql_check must give each case exactly this verdict, rule, offset, text, table set and output SQL, and the hash is sha256 of the output SQL.

cases.why: a plain SELECT of the key and group_name from one table
cases.sql: SELECT o.order_id, o.region AS group_name FROM main.sales.orders o
cases.sql_out: SELECT o.order_id, o.region AS group_name FROM main.sales.orders o

cases.why: a single trailing ; is dropped
cases.sql: SELECT o.order_id, o.region AS group_name FROM main.sales.orders o;
cases.sql_out: SELECT o.order_id, o.region AS group_name FROM main.sales.orders o

cases.why: a single ; at the end, then a comment, is still one statement
cases.sql: SELECT o.order_id, o.region AS group_name FROM main.sales.orders o ; -- done
cases.sql_out: SELECT o.order_id, o.region AS group_name FROM main.sales.orders o

cases.why: a trailing -- comment would eat the wrap's closing parenthesis, so it is removed
cases.sql: SELECT o.order_id, o.region AS group_name FROM main.sales.orders o -- the last line
cases.sql_out: SELECT o.order_id, o.region AS group_name FROM main.sales.orders o

cases.why: a block comment is removed and leaves a space
cases.sql: SELECT /* pick */ o.order_id, o.region AS group_name FROM main.sales.orders o
cases.sql_out: SELECT   o.order_id, o.region AS group_name FROM main.sales.orders o

cases.why: a keyword inside a nested block comment is removed with it
cases.sql: SELECT k /* outer /* inner DELETE */ still DROP */, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k  , g AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: a refused function inside a nested comment never runs
cases.sql: SELECT k /* x /* y */ , secret('s', 'k') AS v */, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k  , g AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: a keyword inside a string is data
cases.sql: SELECT k, CASE WHEN s = 'DELETE' THEN 'x' ELSE 'y' END AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, CASE WHEN s = 'DELETE' THEN 'x' ELSE 'y' END AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: a keyword inside a double-quoted string is data
cases.sql: SELECT k, CASE WHEN s = "DROP TABLE x" THEN 1 ELSE 2 END AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, CASE WHEN s = "DROP TABLE x" THEN 1 ELSE 2 END AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: a keyword in backticks is a column name
cases.sql: SELECT k, `delete` AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, `delete` AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: a doubled backtick stays inside the name, so DELETE is part of it
cases.sql: SELECT `k`` DELETE` AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT `k`` DELETE` AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: a backslash-escaped quote stays inside the string
cases.sql: SELECT k, "a\" DROP" AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, "a\" DROP" AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: a ; inside a string is data
cases.sql: SELECT k, concat(a, ';', b) AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, concat(a, ';', b) AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: a ; inside backticks is part of a name
cases.sql: SELECT k, `a;b` AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, `a;b` AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: a ? inside a string is no parameter
cases.sql: SELECT k, CASE WHEN q = '?' THEN 'a' ELSE 'b' END AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, CASE WHEN q = '?' THEN 'a' ELSE 'b' END AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: backticks around each part, one holding a dot
cases.sql: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM `main`.`my.schema`.`orders`
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM `main`.`my.schema`.`orders`

cases.why: table names are recorded in lower case
cases.sql: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM Main.Sales.Orders
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM Main.Sales.Orders

cases.why: a LEFT JOIN records both tables
cases.sql: SELECT o.k, c.segment AS group_name FROM a.b.orders o LEFT JOIN a.b.customers c ON o.cid = c.id
cases.sql_out: SELECT o.k, c.segment AS group_name FROM a.b.orders o LEFT JOIN a.b.customers c ON o.cid = c.id

cases.why: a comma join records both tables
cases.sql: SELECT x.k, y.g AS group_name FROM a.b.x x, a.b.y y WHERE x.id = y.id
cases.sql_out: SELECT x.k, y.g AS group_name FROM a.b.x x, a.b.y y WHERE x.id = y.id

cases.why: JOIN ... USING (columns) is a join, not a table function
cases.sql: SELECT x.k, y.g AS group_name FROM a.b.x JOIN a.b.y USING (id, day)
cases.sql_out: SELECT x.k, y.g AS group_name FROM a.b.x JOIN a.b.y USING (id, day)

cases.why: a LATERAL subquery is read through its own FROM
cases.sql: SELECT x.k, l.m AS group_name FROM a.b.x x JOIN LATERAL (SELECT max(v) AS m FROM a.b.y y WHERE y.id = x.id) l
cases.sql_out: SELECT x.k, l.m AS group_name FROM a.b.x x JOIN LATERAL (SELECT max(v) AS m FROM a.b.y y WHERE y.id = x.id) l

cases.why: a WITH name is read like a table
cases.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT k, region FROM a.b.c) SELECT k, region AS group_name FROM r
cases.sql_out: WITH r AS (SELECT k, region FROM a.b.c) SELECT k, region AS group_name FROM r

cases.why: a later WITH name may read an earlier one
cases.sql: WITH a1 AS (SELECT k, g FROM x.y.z), b1 AS (SELECT * FROM a1) SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM b1
cases.sql_out: WITH a1 AS (SELECT k, g FROM x.y.z), b1 AS (SELECT * FROM a1) SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM b1

cases.why: a WITH name with a column list
cases.sql: WITH t (k, g) AS (SELECT id, region FROM a.b.c) SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM t
cases.sql_out: WITH t (k, g) AS (SELECT id, region FROM a.b.c) SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM t

cases.why: a WITH name that matches the last part of a real table reads the WITH
cases.sql: WITH orders AS (SELECT * FROM main.sales.orders WHERE amount > 0) SELECT id AS k, region AS group_name FROM orders
cases.sql_out: WITH orders AS (SELECT * FROM main.sales.orders WHERE amount > 0) SELECT id AS k, region AS group_name FROM orders

cases.why: a WITH inside a WITH body is visible inside that body
cases.sql: WITH a1 AS (WITH b1 AS (SELECT id, r FROM x.y.z) SELECT * FROM b1) SELECT id, r AS group_name FROM a1
cases.sql_out: WITH a1 AS (WITH b1 AS (SELECT id, r FROM x.y.z) SELECT * FROM b1) SELECT id, r AS group_name FROM a1

cases.why: a subquery in FROM is read through its own FROM
cases.sql: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM (SELECT id AS k, region AS g FROM a.b.c) s
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM (SELECT id AS k, region AS g FROM a.b.c) s

cases.why: a subquery that starts with FROM
cases.sql: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM (FROM a.b.c SELECT id AS k, r AS g)
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM (FROM a.b.c SELECT id AS k, r AS g)

cases.why: IN (SELECT ...) records its table
cases.sql: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c WHERE k IN (SELECT id FROM a.b.d)
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c WHERE k IN (SELECT id FROM a.b.d)

cases.why: EXISTS (SELECT ...) records its table
cases.sql: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM a.b.d d WHERE d.id = t.k)
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM a.b.d d WHERE d.id = t.k)

cases.why: a scalar subquery in the select list records its table
cases.sql: SELECT k, (SELECT max(name) FROM a.b.names n WHERE n.id = t.g) AS group_name FROM a.b.c t
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, (SELECT max(name) FROM a.b.names n WHERE n.id = t.g) AS group_name FROM a.b.c t

cases.why: FROM inside extract() is no table
cases.sql: SELECT k, CAST(extract(YEAR FROM d) AS STRING) AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, CAST(extract(YEAR FROM d) AS STRING) AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: FROM inside trim() and substring() is no table
cases.sql: SELECT k, substring(trim(BOTH ' ' FROM s) FROM 1 FOR 3) AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, substring(trim(BOTH ' ' FROM s) FROM 1 FOR 3) AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: a colon after a column is a JSON path, not a parameter
cases.sql: SELECT k, raw:region AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, raw:region AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: :: is a cast, not a parameter
cases.sql: SELECT k, region::string AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, region::string AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: VERSION AS OF reads a version of the same table
cases.sql: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c VERSION AS OF 3
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c VERSION AS OF 3

cases.why: @v reads a version of the same table
cases.sql: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c@v3
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c@v3

cases.why: LATERAL VIEW explode is a generator, not a table
cases.sql: SELECT k, t.g AS group_name FROM a.b.c LATERAL VIEW explode(tags) t AS g
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, t.g AS group_name FROM a.b.c LATERAL VIEW explode(tags) t AS g

cases.why: a window function with OVER (PARTITION BY ...)
cases.sql: SELECT k, CASE WHEN rank() OVER (PARTITION BY r ORDER BY v DESC) <= 3 THEN r ELSE 'Other' END AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, CASE WHEN rank() OVER (PARTITION BY r ORDER BY v DESC) <= 3 THEN r ELSE 'Other' END AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: UNION ALL of two tables records both
cases.sql: SELECT k, 'A' AS group_name FROM a.b.c UNION ALL SELECT k, 'B' FROM a.b.d
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, 'A' AS group_name FROM a.b.c UNION ALL SELECT k, 'B' FROM a.b.d

cases.why: a raw string ends at its quote even after a backslash
cases.sql: SELECT k, r'C:\path\' AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, r'C:\path\' AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: an escaped quote hides DELETE inside the string
cases.sql: SELECT k, 'it\'s DELETE' AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, 'it\'s DELETE' AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: two quotes in a row are two strings side by side
cases.sql: SELECT k, 'it''s' AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, 'it''s' AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: letters outside ASCII inside a string
cases.sql: SELECT k, CASE WHEN c = 'Ünïcödé' THEN 'a' ELSE 'b' END AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, CASE WHEN c = 'Ünïcödé' THEN 'a' ELSE 'b' END AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: a table name outside ASCII in backticks is recorded in backticks
cases.sql: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM main.sales.`Ventes_é`
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM main.sales.`Ventes_é`

cases.why: a character outside the basic plane inside a string
cases.sql: SELECT k, '😀' AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, '😀' AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: CR LF line ends become LF
cases.sql:
SELECT k,
  g AS group_name
FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out:
SELECT k,
  g AS group_name
FROM a.b.c

cases.why: space and new lines around the SQL are trimmed
cases.sql: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: number literals with exponents and suffixes
cases.sql: SELECT k, CASE WHEN v > 1.5e3D THEN 'big' WHEN v > .5 THEN 'mid' ELSE 'small' END AS group_name FROM a.b.c WHERE v > 100L AND w < 2.0BD
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, CASE WHEN v > 1.5e3D THEN 'big' WHEN v > .5 THEN 'mid' ELSE 'small' END AS group_name FROM a.b.c WHERE v > 100L AND w < 2.0BD

cases.why: a /*+ hint */ is a comment Inspire removes
cases.sql: SELECT /*+ BROADCAST(c) */ o.k, c.g AS group_name FROM a.b.o o JOIN a.b.cc c ON o.id = c.id
cases.sql_out: SELECT   o.k, c.g AS group_name FROM a.b.o o JOIN a.b.cc c ON o.id = c.id

cases.why: REPLACE in backticks is the string function, not the statement
cases.sql: SELECT k, `replace`(g, 'a', 'b') AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, `replace`(g, 'a', 'b') AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: UPDATE, DELETE and SET inside longer names are names
cases.sql: SELECT k, concat(updated_at, deleted_flag, settings, user_list) AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, concat(updated_at, deleted_flag, settings, user_list) AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: a column named secret is no call
cases.sql: SELECT k, secret AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, secret AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: a lambda inside transform()
cases.sql: SELECT k, array_join(transform(tags, x -> upper(x)), ',') AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, array_join(transform(tags, x -> upper(x)), ',') AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: a table alias with a column list
cases.sql: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c AS t (k, g)
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c AS t (k, g)

cases.why: TABLESAMPLE reads part of the same table
cases.sql: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c TABLESAMPLE (10 PERCENT)
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c TABLESAMPLE (10 PERCENT)

cases.why: map and struct access
cases.sql: SELECT k, coalesce(attrs['region'], info.region, 'None') AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, coalesce(attrs['region'], info.region, 'None') AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: exactly 20,000 characters is allowed
cases.sql: SELECT k, '' AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT k, '' AS group_name FROM a.b.c

cases.why: tabs between words
cases.sql: SELECT	k,	g	AS	group_name	FROM	a.b.c
cases.sql_out: SELECT	k,	g	AS	group_name	FROM	a.b.c

cases.why: nothing to run
cases.text: The grouping SQL is empty; write one SELECT that returns the record key columns and group_name.

cases.why: a comment alone is empty
cases.sql: -- nothing here
cases.text: The grouping SQL is empty; write one SELECT that returns the record key columns and group_name.

cases.why: a lone ; is no statement
cases.text: The grouping SQL is empty; write one SELECT that returns the record key columns and group_name.

cases.why: 20,001 characters is over the limit
cases.sql: SELECT k, '' AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.text: The grouping SQL is 20001 characters long; Inspire takes at most 20000 characters.

cases.why: two SELECTs
cases.sql: SELECT 1; SELECT 2
cases.text: The grouping SQL holds more than one statement: there is a ; at character 8. Write one SELECT; Inspire drops only a single ; at the very end.

cases.why: a DROP after the ;
cases.sql: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c; DROP TABLE a.b.c
cases.text: The grouping SQL holds more than one statement: there is a ; at character 36. Write one SELECT; Inspire drops only a single ; at the very end.

cases.why: two ; at the end
cases.sql: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c;;
cases.text: The grouping SQL holds more than one statement: there is a ; at character 36. Write one SELECT; Inspire drops only a single ; at the very end.

cases.why: a ; hidden after a comment still ends a statement
cases.sql: SELECT 1 /* ; */ ; DELETE FROM a.b.c
cases.text: The grouping SQL holds more than one statement: there is a ; at character 17. Write one SELECT; Inspire drops only a single ; at the very end.

cases.why: an INSERT
cases.sql: INSERT INTO a.b.c SELECT 1
cases.text: The grouping SQL must start with SELECT or WITH; it starts with INSERT.

cases.why: an UPDATE
cases.sql: UPDATE a.b.c SET g = 1
cases.text: The grouping SQL must start with SELECT or WITH; it starts with UPDATE.

cases.why: a DELETE
cases.sql: DELETE FROM a.b.c
cases.text: The grouping SQL must start with SELECT or WITH; it starts with DELETE.

cases.why: a MERGE
cases.sql: MERGE INTO a.b.c USING a.b.d ON 1 = 1 WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE
cases.text: The grouping SQL must start with SELECT or WITH; it starts with MERGE.

cases.why: a SELECT in parentheses does not start with SELECT
cases.sql: (SELECT k FROM a.b.c)
cases.text: The grouping SQL must start with SELECT or WITH; it starts with (.

cases.why: EXPLAIN
cases.sql: EXPLAIN SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.text: The grouping SQL must start with SELECT or WITH; it starts with EXPLAIN.

cases.why: SHOW
cases.sql: SHOW TABLES IN a.b
cases.text: The grouping SQL must start with SELECT or WITH; it starts with SHOW.

cases.why: VALUES
cases.sql: VALUES (1, 'a')
cases.text: The grouping SQL must start with SELECT or WITH; it starts with VALUES.

cases.why: FROM-first at the top
cases.sql: FROM a.b.c SELECT k, g AS group_name
cases.text: The grouping SQL must start with SELECT or WITH; it starts with FROM.

cases.why: a DELETE on the line after a comment
cases.sql:
SELECT k FROM a.b.c -- harmless
WHERE k IN (DELETE FROM a.b.c)
cases.text: The grouping SQL uses DELETE at character 44, which Inspire refuses so the SQL can only read; if it is a column or table name, put it in backticks.

cases.why: a DROP after a nested comment closes
cases.sql: SELECT k /* a /* b */ c */ DROP FROM a.b.c
cases.text: The grouping SQL uses DROP at character 27, which Inspire refuses so the SQL can only read; if it is a column or table name, put it in backticks.

cases.why: a nested comment that never closes hides the rest
cases.sql: SELECT k, 1 AS group_name /* /* */ , secret('a', 'b') AS s FROM a.b.c
cases.text: The grouping SQL has a comment that never ends, starting at character 26.

cases.why: a Cyrillic E in DELETE
cases.sql: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c WHERE x = 1 OR DЕLETE
cases.text: The grouping SQL has the character U+0415 at character 53, which Inspire refuses outside a string or a name in backticks.

cases.why: a Cyrillic E in SELECT
cases.sql: SЕLECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.text: The grouping SQL has the character U+0415 at character 1, which Inspire refuses outside a string or a name in backticks.

cases.why: a full-width semicolon
cases.sql: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c； DROP TABLE a.b.c
cases.text: The grouping SQL has the character U+FF1B at character 36, which Inspire refuses outside a string or a name in backticks.

cases.why: a no-break space between words
cases.sql: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.text: The grouping SQL has the character U+00A0 at character 6, which Inspire refuses outside a string or a name in backticks.

cases.why: a zero-width space between words
cases.sql: SELECT k,​ g AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.text: The grouping SQL has the character U+200B at character 9, which Inspire refuses outside a string or a name in backticks.

cases.why: a right-to-left override, even inside a string
cases.sql: SELECT k, '‮' AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.text: The grouping SQL has the character U+202E at character 11, which Inspire refuses anywhere in the SQL.

cases.why: a NUL character, even inside a string
cases.sql: SELECT k, 'a�b' AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.text: The grouping SQL has the character U+0000 at character 12, which Inspire refuses anywhere in the SQL.

cases.why: half of a surrogate pair, even inside a string
cases.sql: SELECT k, '�' AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.text: The grouping SQL has the character U+D800 at character 11, which Inspire refuses anywhere in the SQL.

cases.why: a form feed between words
cases.sql: SELECT k,  g AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.text: The grouping SQL has the character U+000C at character 9, which Inspire refuses anywhere in the SQL.

cases.why: a # outside a string
cases.sql: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c # note
cases.text: The grouping SQL has the character '#' at character 37, which Inspire refuses outside a string or a name in backticks.

cases.why: a brace outside a string
cases.sql: SELECT k, {g} AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.text: The grouping SQL has the character '{' at character 10, which Inspire refuses outside a string or a name in backticks.

cases.why: a backslash outside a string
cases.sql: SELECT k, g \ 2 AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.text: The grouping SQL has the character '\' at character 12, which Inspire refuses outside a string or a name in backticks.

cases.why: ${...} inside a string is substituted before Spark reads the SQL
cases.sql: SELECT k, '${spark.secret.key}' AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.text: The grouping SQL holds ${ at character 11; Inspire refuses variable substitution anywhere, even inside a string.

cases.why: ${...} inside a comment
cases.sql: SELECT k, g AS group_name /* ${x} */ FROM a.b.c
cases.text: The grouping SQL holds ${ at character 29; Inspire refuses variable substitution anywhere, even inside a string.

cases.why: ${...} inside backticks
cases.sql: SELECT k, `${x}` AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.text: The grouping SQL holds ${ at character 11; Inspire refuses variable substitution anywhere, even inside a string.

cases.why: a ? parameter
cases.sql: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c WHERE k = ?
cases.text: The grouping SQL uses a parameter at character 47; write the value itself, since Inspire runs the SQL with no parameters.

cases.why: a :name parameter after =
cases.sql: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c WHERE k = :k
cases.text: The grouping SQL uses a parameter at character 47; write the value itself, since Inspire runs the SQL with no parameters.

cases.why: a :name parameter right after WHERE
cases.sql: SELECT k, g AS group_name FROM a.b.c WHERE :flag
cases.text: The grouping SQL uses a parameter at character 43; write the value itself, since Inspire runs the SQL with no parameters.

cases.why: a :name parameter as an argument
cases.sql: SELECT k, coalesce(:g, 'x') AS group_name FROM a.b.c
cases.text: The grouping SQL uses a parameter at character 19; write the value itself, since Inspire runs the SQL with no parameters.
